title: Customer escalation war-room: Aurora Pay outage prep + notes
agenda: Quick sync: current customer impact (who, what, scope)
Rollback/fallback plan & communication draft for Aurora Pay ops
Action items and next sync cadence
content:
Purpose: prep + live notes for the Aurora Pay war-room (customer experiencing intermittent 500s and large tail latencies in hosted API since 03/10 04:20 UTC). Goal: triage, mitigate customer impact, own comms, and create a clear action list.

Summary (high-level):
- Reported at 04:22 UTC by Aurora monitoring: spike in error rate from 0.1% -> ~6% for /v1/generate.
- Customer impact: payment processing jobs retrying; Aurora reports ~15% of their authorization calls failing. Business impact: delayed settlements and customer complaints.
- Observed by us: increased queuing on GPU pool dedicated to hosted region us-west-2; elevated latency for long-sequence requests (>1024 tokens).
- Known constraints: Aurora uses large-batch streaming with pinned model "openlm-large-v1" and sometimes uses function-calls.

Initial timeline (as reported / observed):
- 04:20 UTC: Aurora alert triggered (first spike).
- 04:23 UTC: Customer support received escalation (Aurora ops).
- 04:28 UTC: On-call SRE pinged, started smoke checks.
- 04:35 UTC: Serving runtime trace shows KV cache eviction events and memory pressure on pool gpu-usw2-pool-3.
- 04:40 UTC: CS opened JIRA CS-4271 and created Confluence incident page.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Memory pressure / cache eviction on gpu-usw2-pool-3 triggered increased cold-starts and longer decode times for long sequences. Related: recent autoscaler change (merged 03/08) that tightened headroom.
2) A bad influx of very long requests from Aurora (sequence length distribution change) caused blocking and queueing; batch size configuration combined with their workload led to starvation.
3) Regression in kernel selection for the quantized path for the specific model variant; less likely but plausible given updated kernel selection heuristics last week.

Immediate mitigations (short-term, aim for <30 min):
- Throttle long-sequence requests for Aurora at the API gateway (soft limit on tokens/request) — TEMP until root cause found. Owner: Maya. Due: 04:55 UTC.
- Increase headroom on gpu-usw2-pool-3 by temporarily disabling aggressive scale-in (bump min replicas + allocate 2 spare GPUs). Owner: Jordan Li. Due: 05:05 UTC.
- Force warm KV-cache for Aurora pinned model using a synthetic prefix warmup if needed (work with serving-runtime). Owner: Ravi Shah. Due: 05:10 UTC.
- Route Aurora traffic to fallback compatible model variant in another pool/region (us-west-1) for critical traffic only. Owner: Alex Kim (SRE) + Ravi. Due: 05:20 UTC.
- Draft customer-facing comms: short explanation + ETA and mitigation steps. Owner: Sofia Martinez. Due: 05:00 UTC.

Rollback / fallback plan:
- If mitigations do not reduce error rate to <1% in 30 minutes, shift all Aurora critical traffic to dedicated fallback model variant in us-west-1 with reserved capacity. Notify Aurora ops and confirm any latency expectations. Owner: Alex Kim. 

Escalation path (contacts):
- SRE on-call: Alex Kim (pager: +1-555-0101)
- Serving runtime lead: Ravi Shah (Slack DM), backup: Priyanka (eng-team)
- Infra: Jordan Li
- Customer Success / Account Exec: Sofia Martinez
- CS escalation manager: Maya Patel

Customer comms (draft bullets):
- Acknowledge issue and impact: "We are seeing elevated error rates for some of your generate requests affecting authorizations. Our team is actively mitigating and prioritizing your traffic."
- Immediate actions we are taking: throttle long-run requests, increase headroom, warm caches, route critical calls to fallback pool.
- ETA: first measurable improvement expected within 15–30 minutes; next update at +30 minutes.
- Ask of customer: if possible, temporarily reduce very long sequence usage for time-critical paths; provide a replay sample of failing request IDs (Aurora will supply).

Open questions / unknowns (notes-to-self):
- Is Aurora using any recent client-side SDK changes that changed tokenization? (ask Aurora dev).
- Did the autoscaler change on 03/08 have unintended side effects for pooling? Need to review merge.
- Are function-calls causing larger-than-expected token payloads? (check request logs).

Live notes (post-meeting):
- 04:50 UTC: throttling rule applied for >1,200 tokens; immediate drop in queue length observed. Error rate reduced from 6% -> 2.1% in 4 minutes.
- 05:03 UTC: scaled pool headroom increased; tail latencies improving but still occasional 95th percentile spikes.
- 05:12 UTC: warmed KV cache; observe fewer cold starts for pinned model.
- 05:22 UTC: partial traffic shift to us-west-1 fallback for critical endpoints. Aurora reports authorization success rate improved to 98.5% (their monitoring).

Post-meeting summary (short):
- Mitigations worked incrementally: throttling + headroom + cache warming + partial routing brought errors down from ~6% to ~1.5% within 45 minutes.
- Root cause likely combination: sudden increase in long requests from Aurora + reduced autoscaler headroom. Kernel regression not ruled out; queued for post-incident deep dive.
action_items: Maya Patel - Apply API gateway soft throttle for >1200 tokens and monitor error rate (due 2026-03-10)
Jordan Li - Increase min replicas on gpu-usw2-pool-3 + allocate 2 spare GPUs (due 2026-03-10)
Ravi Shah - Run KV-cache warmup script for Aurora pinned model, monitor cold-starts (due 2026-03-10)
Alex Kim - Execute traffic routing to fallback pool in us-west-1 for critical endpoints and validate success rate (due 2026-03-10)
Sofia Martinez - Send customer-facing status update and collect sample failing request IDs from Aurora (due 2026-03-10)
Maya Patel - Create post-incident follow-up ticket: deep root cause analysis and autoscaler config review (JIRA linked) (due 2026-03-12)
Ravi Shah - Check recent kernel selection commits (last 7 days) for regressions and report findings (due 2026-03-12)
Jordan Li - Prepare capacity plan for long-tail events (recommend min buffer % for pools) (due 2026-03-15)
All - Daily update in incident channel for next 3 days or until RCA completed (owner: Maya)
notes: Tone: keep comms concise and non-technical for ops; CC eng leads for technical appendices. This doc is a working scratchpad — copy into Confluence incident page for the formal timeline/RCA. Reminders: capture request IDs, traces, and exact kernel/commit hashes if we pursue regression.\n\nFollow-up meeting: daily 09:00 UTC cadence until RCA closed; next sync 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC.
